sentence: The endings themselves, for every one of these irregular stems, still closely echo the [regular -er/-ir preterite set](/spanish-preterite-endings/), with -e and -o in place of -í and -ió for yo and él.
note: Target lists the regular -er/-ir endings; source explicitly qualifies the irregular substitution in yo/él and its own j-stem exceptions.
target_quote: answer: 'For -ar verbs, the six endings run -é (yo), -aste (tú), -ó (él/ella), -amos (nosotros), -asteis (vosotros), and -aron (ellos), giving forms like hablé and hablamos. -Er and -ir verbs, by contrast, use one shared set: -í for yo, -iste for tú, -ió for él/ella, -imos for nosotros, -isteis for vosotros, -ieron for ellos (comí/viví, comiste/viviste, comió/vivió, comimos/vivimos, comisteis/vivisteis, comieron/vivieron).',
